skill.name: video-inpainting
skill.description: Use RunComfy video edit models to repair or replace selected regions across video frames. The skill routes requests by edit type and explains when to use CLI endpoints or ComfyUI workflows.
skill.summary: Route video inpainting requests through RunComfy models with practical CLI guidance.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown backticks and documentation links. Confirmed risks are limited to documented RunComfy CLI execution, external video processing, and watermark removal abuse potential. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: RunComfy CLI execution and installation guidance
remediation.suggestion: Keep npm or npx installation as explicit human setup, pin trusted package versions, and require confirmation before running RunComfy jobs.

remediation.issue: External processing of user videos and prompts
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit consent step before sending media to RunComfy, especially for private or sensitive clips.

remediation.issue: Watermark and logo removal can be abused
remediation.suggestion: State that removal is only for content the user owns or has permission to edit, and refuse third-party watermark removal.

remediation.issue: API token storage needs clear handling guidance
remediation.suggestion: Continue documenting token path and file mode, and recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for ephemeral or shared environments.

content.value_statement: Region edits across moving video frames are hard to route and prompt consistently. This skill selects a RunComfy path and gives safe prompt patterns for cleanup or replacement.
actual_capabilities: Routes prompt-driven region edits to Wan 2-7 Edit-Video as the default path.
Explains when Lucy Edit Restyle or Seedream Edit-Sequential better matches the request.
Provides RunComfy CLI setup and invocation guidance for video edit jobs.
Points users to ComfyUI workflows when mask propagation or temporal consistency matters.
Documents token handling, outbound endpoints, file size limits, and relevant exit codes.
limitations: It does not provide pixel-perfect masks through the CLI path.
Long clips and motion-heavy fills can lose temporal consistency.
It requires a RunComfy account, API token, and external cloud processing.
It should only remove logos or watermarks from content the user owns or may edit.

use_cases.title: Clean Short Video Clips
use_cases.description: Remove a distracting object from a short clip while preserving the rest of the scene.

use_cases.title: Prepare Campaign Assets
use_cases.description: Patch small regions in product or social videos before final review.

use_cases.title: Automate Edit Routing
use_cases.description: Choose a RunComfy route for repeated region edits in a CLI workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Object Cleanup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup with one visible target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the video-inpainting skill to remove the visible object from my clip. Preserve the rest of the frame and match the background.

prompt_templates.title: Region-Specific Repair
prompt_templates.scenario: A known region needs careful cleanup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use RunComfy to remove the object in the bottom-right corner of my source video. Keep lighting, camera motion, and all other content unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Select the Best Route
prompt_templates.scenario: The user needs help choosing a model path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Wan 2-7, Lucy Edit Restyle, and Seedream Edit-Sequential for this clip. Recommend the route before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Controlled Fallback
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow planning for difficult clips.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a frame-stack or ComfyUI fallback when the CLI edit lacks temporal consistency. Include quality checks, retry limits, and user confirmation points.

output_examples.input: A user asks to remove a passing background person from a short clip.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Wan 2-7 Edit-Video, drafts a preservation-first prompt, and explains when to retry with mask-aware workflows.

output_examples.input: A user needs exact replacement of a product label across motion.
output_examples.output: The skill flags the need for stronger control, suggests a frame-stack or ComfyUI workflow, and warns about brand consistency checks.

output_examples.input: A user asks why the result changed the whole frame.
output_examples.output: The skill advises narrowing the spatial description, adding preservation language, and making one edit per run.

best_practices: Confirm the user owns or may edit the source video before removing marks, logos, or people.
Use one targeted change per run and preserve all unrelated content in the prompt.
Use ComfyUI workflows when masks, segmentation tracking, or long-clip consistency are required.
anti_patterns: Do not remove third-party watermarks, attribution marks, or copyright notices without authorization.
Do not process private videos through RunComfy unless the user consents to external processing.
Do not combine unrelated edits in one prompt when temporal consistency matters.

faq.question: Does this skill edit videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI and RunComfy cloud endpoints for model processing.

faq.question: Which model does it use first?
faq.answer: It uses Wan 2-7 Edit-Video for prompt-driven region edits unless another route fits better.

faq.question: Can it use precise masks?
faq.answer: The CLI path is prompt-driven. The skill points to ComfyUI workflows for mask propagation and temporal consistency.

faq.question: Can it remove watermarks?
faq.answer: Only when the user owns the content or has permission. It should not help remove third-party ownership or attribution marks.

faq.question: What inputs are needed?
faq.answer: The user needs a source video URL, a clear region description, and a preservation-focused edit instruction.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: RunComfy downloads generated files to the selected output directory after the remote job completes.
